claim: The 'send-prop-test-ping' Tier-1 system-action, documented in three independent places as journaling nothing, ALWAYS writes a real 'emitted' ticket row into the live trade_journal.db for the account's real routed symbol/direction, which can silently suppress the next genuine trade signal.
evidence: Three independent 'nothing journaled' claims: (1) scripts/prop/send_test_ping.py:11-13 docstring: "it calls the emitter DIRECTLY (not the full execute path), so NOTHING is journaled and no exchange socket is ever opened"; its printed result.note (lines 142-146) repeats "TEST ping only — nothing journaled, no exchange socket opened."; (2) scripts/ops/send_prop_test_ping_action.sh:7-8: "It calls the emitter directly (not the execute path), so NOTHING is journaled and no exchange socket is opened."; (3) docs/claude/system-actions.md:255-257: "send-prop-test-ping — fires one synthetic TEST prop ticket through the real emit_prop_signal path (FCM + prop Telegram bot); notify-only, nothing journaled". All three are false for EVERY invocation. Read src/prop/breakout_executor.py::emit_prop_ticket in full: the journal write (`prop_journal.record_ticket({..., "status": "emitted", "valid_until": ...})`) runs unconditionally whenever `leg.decision == "place"`, in a try/except block that executes BEFORE the `if _emitter is not None: _emitter(...) else: emit_prop_signal(...)` branch. The `_emitter` parameter (injected by send_test_ping.py only when --no-push or --no-telegram is passed, send_test_ping.py:118-124) substitutes only the notification-delivery step, never the journal write above it. So both send_test_ping.py's default invocation — exactly how send_prop_test_ping_action.sh calls it: `"${TEST_PING}" --symbol "${SYMBOL}" --strategy "${STRATEGY}"` — and its --no-push/--no-telegram invocation write the same real journal row. That 'emitted' row is then read by `_reticket_suppress_reason` (breakout_executor.py:69-130), which suppresses (journals a 'suppressed' row, sends no push) any subsequent `emit_prop_ticket` call for the SAME (account_id, symbol, direction) whose emitted ticket's `valid_until` has not passed — the suppression key does not include strategy, so the test ping's synthetic strategy label ('trend_donchian_sol [TEST PING — ignore, not a real signal]') does not protect a real signal on the same symbol+direction. The action's own defaults (account=breakout_1, symbol=SOLUSDT, side=long, timeframe=1h -> ~60min TTL via breakout_ticket.py's ttl_bars*_TF_MINUTES with breakout_routing.yaml's ttl_bars=1.0) are exactly config/prop_rulesets/breakout_routing.yaml's real live-routed leg (strategies: [trend_donchian_sol, trend_donchian_eth], symbols: SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT).
expected: A Tier-1 action documented and comment-labelled as having zero mutation effect on the live journal, 'safe to run any number of times', should not be able to alter the outcome of a real subsequent trade signal.
actual: Every invocation writes a real 'emitted' ticket to the canonical money DB, and with the action's own defaults that row exactly matches the account's real routed strategy/symbol/direction, so a genuine trend_donchian_sol/eth signal on SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT firing within roughly the next hour is silently suppressed (journaled only as an inconspicuous 'suppressed' row, never surfaced to the operator as a dropped trade).
population: Read src/prop/breakout_executor.py, src/prop/breakout_ticket.py, scripts/prop/send_test_ping.py, scripts/ops/send_prop_test_ping_action.sh, and the docs/claude/system-actions.md row in full (n=5 files, this audit lane). Confirmed both the default and --no-push/--no-telegram code paths independently. tests/ has zero coverage of send_test_ping.py (no test_prop_send_test_ping*.py exists), so this was never caught by CI.
fix: Exclude test-ping tickets from _reticket_suppress_reason's status check (or route them through a path that never writes status='emitted'), then correct the three now-false 'nothing journaled' claims and add a regression test.
proposed_fix: Tier-2 (touches live order-path suppression state, so operator-reviewed before shipping): either (a) give emit_prop_ticket a test-mode that still renders+sends the ticket but journals it under a status _reticket_suppress_reason explicitly excludes (e.g. 'test_ping'), or (b) keep the journal write (so the report-back JSON still works for a human drill) but exclude test tickets from the suppression status check — either way, correct all three now-false 'nothing journaled' claims and add tests/test_prop_send_test_ping.py asserting prop_journal.list_tickets()/the suppression guard are unaffected by a test-ping invocation.
detector: None exists today (no tests/test_prop_send_test_ping*.py). Proposed: the regression test above.

claim: src/prop/prop_sl_tp_alert.py — the only module that alerts the operator in real time when price crosses an open Breakout position's SL or TP — has zero test coverage anywhere in the repository.
location: src/prop/prop_sl_tp_alert.py (224 lines, whole module); consumed by src/prop/prop_fills_staleness.py's crossed_unreported detector
evidence: `ls tests/ | grep -i sl_tp` returns nothing; `grep -rln 'run_prop_sl_tp_alert|_sl_crossed|_tp_crossed' tests/` returns nothing (both reconfirmed directly by this session). The only hit for the module name in tests/ is a docstring mention in tests/test_prop_fills_staleness.py:287. tests/test_prop_fills_staleness.py:413 monkeypatches `fs._sl_tp_state` with a synthetic dict rather than ever calling the real module, so the state-file contract (`{position_key: {sl_alerted_at, tp_alerted_at}}`) is never exercised end-to-end either. A manual sanity run (planted an ETH short with SL 2050, fed a price of 2060) confirmed the code currently behaves correctly (fires once, persists state, does not re-fire) — this is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated live bug.
expected: Given this module's own docstring states the bot has no broker feed and this is the mechanism that tells the operator to go check, and every sibling prop module (prop_balance, prop_monitor_pulse, prop_fills_staleness, prop_expiry_prompt, prop_invalidation_prompt, prop_status_request) has a substantial dedicated test file, direct unit tests for the one-shot-per-level latch, state persistence/pruning, and crossing logic were expected.
actual: None exist. A future edit that breaks the one-shot latch (double-alerting — this repo's own named P1 'desensitized alarm' pattern) or the persisted-state logic (silently stops alerting) would ship with no CI signal.
population: n=1 module (224 lines) read in full; zero references confirmed via two independent greps across tests/ (by filename and by function name) plus one live sanity-check run of the module's core loop.
blast_radius: This module is a load-bearing dependency of a second safety mechanism: prop_fills_staleness.py's crossed_unreported detector (described in its own docstring as the leading indicator for a book that traded without being reported) reads prop_sl_tp_alert's persisted state directly. A silent regression here degrades both the immediate operator alert AND the staleness detector's early-warning arm on a $5k eval account where a limit breach is permanent and un-appealable.
fix: Add tests/test_prop_sl_tp_alert.py covering crossing detection (long+short), one-alert-per-level, state pruning on close, the price-fetch-failure path, and an integration test wiring its real on-disk state into prop_fills_staleness.assess_crossings.
proposed_fix: Add tests/test_prop_sl_tp_alert.py covering: (1) SL/TP crossing detection for both long and short at the boundary; (2) one-alert-per-level-per-position-lifetime (no re-fire on a second tick still past the level); (3) state pruning when a position closes; (4) the price-fetch-failure path leaves state unchanged and doesn't crash; (5) an integration test running the real run_prop_sl_tp_alert and feeding its actual on-disk state file into prop_fills_staleness.assess_crossings, replacing (or supplementing) the synthetic-dict monkeypatch at test_prop_fills_staleness.py:413.
detector: None today; the proposed test suite above is the detector.

fix: Add 3 tests constructing rulesets with a non-terminal drawdown_breach, drawdown_type: trailing, and max_drawdown_pct: None respectively, asserting run_montecarlo(...)['dd_model_state'] is not_terminal / unmodelled_trailing / no_limit_declared.

claim: config/accounts.yaml's breakout_1.risk block claims the live ticket sizes from config/prop_rulesets/breakout_routing.yaml's risk_pct, but the live executor path never reads that key at all.
location: config/accounts.yaml:1827-1834 (breakout_1.risk.risk_pct comment); config/prop_rulesets/breakout_routing.yaml:12 (the unread key); scripts/prop/emit_breakout_ticket.py:37 (its only reader)
evidence: config/accounts.yaml:1831-1834: "risk_pct: 0.015  # 1.5% — the validated best-EV cell (the ticket sizes from breakout_routing.yaml risk_pct, in PERCENT; this fraction is the PropRiskManager mirror)." `grep -rn 'routing.get("risk_pct")|routing\[.risk_pct.\]' src/ scripts/` returns zero matches. The live path is breakout_executor.emit_prop_ticket -> multi_account_ticket.build_account_leg -> account_rulesets.unit_for_account, which reads risk_pct from account['risk']['risk_pct'] (accounts.yaml itself, this exact key) or the flat account['risk_pct'] fallback — never from breakout_routing.yaml. breakout_routing.yaml's top-level risk_pct: 1.5 key is read by exactly one caller: scripts/prop/emit_breakout_ticket.py:37, a Tier-1 demo CLI that 'places NO order', not the live path. tests/test_breakout_prop_wiring.py:125 asserts unit.risk_pct derives from accounts.yaml (0.015 -> 1.5), confirming accounts.yaml is the real source.
expected: The comment describing where live sizing comes from should name the actual source (accounts.yaml's own risk.risk_pct), or the live path should read breakout_routing.yaml if that is meant to be authoritative.
actual: The comment has the causality backwards: accounts.yaml's risk_pct is claimed to mirror breakout_routing.yaml, when breakout_routing.yaml's risk_pct is actually an orphaned duplicate nothing in the live path reads. The two values currently agree (both 1.5%), so there is no live sizing error today, but the dead key is a landmine: an operator or agent editing breakout_routing.yaml's risk_pct expecting to change live ticket sizing would see no effect, silently.
population: Grepped risk_pct across all of src/prop/*.py (10 files) and scripts/prop/*.py (9 files); confirmed against PR #13154 (open, unmerged, read via its diff) which adds a new sizing: block to breakout.yaml and src/prop/prop_sizing.py — its flat mode still bases off unit.risk_pct (accounts.yaml), so the dead breakout_routing.yaml key stays dead there too, unchanged by #13154.
fix: Rewrite the accounts.yaml comment to name the real source; clarify breakout_routing.yaml's risk_pct is demo-CLI-only.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the accounts.yaml comment to state the real source (this file's own risk.risk_pct) and clarify that breakout_routing.yaml's risk_pct is read only by the standalone demo CLI (scripts/prop/emit_breakout_ticket.py), not the live executor. Optionally rename the routing.yaml key (e.g. demo_default_risk_pct) so its scope is unambiguous.
detector: None today. Proposed: a script asserting every top-level key in breakout_routing.yaml is referenced by breakout_executor.py or multi_account_ticket.py, or is explicitly listed as demo-CLI-only.

claim: prop_fills_staleness.py silently collapses 'accounts.yaml could not be read' into 'there are no declared prop accounts to check' for any account that is currently flat, contradicting the module's own 'states never collapsed' design principle and the more careful handling of the identical situation in the sibling module prop_status_request.py.
evidence: src/prop/prop_fills_staleness.py:596-601: `declared = declared_prop_account_ids(live_only=True) or []` collapses the documented three-state return of declared_prop_account_ids (None='could not look' vs []='looked, none exist', per src/prop/prop_identity.py's own docstring) with NO log line at all when the function returns None without raising (the `except` block only logs, at DEBUG, when the import/call itself raises — a plain None return is silent). Contrast with src/prop/prop_status_request.py:513-522, which does the identical read and explicitly logs a WARNING naming the degraded coverage ('covering only accounts with a currently-open prop position') when declared is None.
expected: A config-read failure for the account-enumeration half of this detector should be at least as visible as the sibling module's handling of the same failure.
actual: It is invisible for a None return (no log at all) and DEBUG-only for a raised exception (effectively invisible in production log retention), and produces no distinguishable state in the returned summary dict.
population: n=1 call site read in full alongside its sibling in prop_status_request.py (both read in full by this audit).
blast_radius: Narrow — requires accounts.yaml to be simultaneously unreadable AND the affected account to hold no open position (so it isn't captured by the position-holding fallback in the same union) for detector B (balance_moved_unreported) to silently stop being asked about on that account. Not user-visible today; would only manifest under a config-loader outage.
fix: Log at WARNING when declared_prop_account_ids returns None (mirroring prop_status_request.py), and surface a config_unavailable flag in the returned summary dict.
proposed_fix: Mirror prop_status_request.py's handling: log at WARNING when declared_prop_account_ids returns None (not just on a raised exception), and consider surfacing a config_unavailable flag in the returned summary dict so a reviewer running the health-review skill can see the degraded-coverage state rather than a clean run.
detector: None today. Proposed: a test asserting a WARNING is logged when declared_prop_account_ids is mocked to return None.
